title: A few small pockets left
quote: There are only a few small pockets left.
quoteBy: Adolf Hitler, speech to Nazi Party veterans, Munich, 8 November 1942

facts.text: On 8 November 1942, Hitler gave his yearly speech in Munich to Nazi Party veterans, the 'Old Fighters', on the anniversary of the 1923 Beer Hall Putsch.
The same day, Allied troops landed in French North Africa in Operation Torch.
He said he had wanted to reach the Volga at one particular city, and claimed Germany now had it. In the Domarus translation: 'There are only a few small pockets left.'
He added that he did not want 'a second Verdun' and would rather take the rest with small assault groups, and that no ship came up the Volga any more.
Soviet attacks surrounded the German Sixth Army at Stalingrad on 23 November 1942, which went unreported in the German press.
Operation Uranus, the Soviet counteroffensive, opened on 19 November 1942.

sources.title: Hitler's speech on 8 November 1942 (Domarus translation), German Propaganda Archive, Calvin University

declassified.fact: The 'small pockets' line was reprinted in the Nazi wall newspaper Parole der Woche on 25 November 1942, two days after the Sixth Army had been surrounded.

body:
The same day the Allies landed in North Africa, Hitler stood up in a Munich beer hall and told the Nazi Party faithful that Stalingrad was won.

8 November 1942. It was his yearly speech for the anniversary of the 1923 Beer Hall Putsch. He said he had wanted to reach the Volga at one particular city, and now he had it:

"There are only a few small pockets left."

Those pockets held. Eleven days later the Red Army struck back. By 23 November the German Sixth Army was surrounded inside the city, and German newspapers never reported it.
